source_text: Seraphim stabant in circuitu, sex alae uni. Duabus velabant faciem Dei, duabus pedes, duabus volabant. Clamabant: Sanctus Sanctus Sanctus — mysterium Trinitatis. Haec duo Seraphim Dominus Iesus et Spiritus sanctus. Operiebant faciem — exordium Dei ignotum; pedes — novissimum incomprehensibile; sola media videntur. Gloria Trinitati. Amen.
pass_a_gloss: Seraphim were-standing in circuit, six wings to-one. With-two they-were-veiling face of-God, with-two feet, with-two they-were-flying. They-were-crying: Holy Holy Holy — mystery of-Trinity. These two Seraphim Lord Jesus and Spirit holy. They-were-covering face — beginning of-God unknown; feet — last incomprehensible; only middle-things are-seen. Glory to-Trinity. Amen.
pass_b_english: [[Seraphim stood about him, six wings to each >> Bible:Isaiah 6:2]]. With two they veiled God’s face, with two his feet, with two they flew. They cried [[Holy, Holy, Holy >> Bible:Isaiah 6:3]] — Trinity’s mystery. Origen reads the two Seraphim as the Lord Jesus and the Holy Spirit. They cover the face — God’s beginning unknown; the feet — the last things incomprehensible; only the middle is seen. Glory to the Trinity. Amen.
notes: True OET; no Scheck FOTC Isaiah/Ezekiel.
